text: In chromotography technique, the purification of compound is independent of :
options: Mobility or flow of solvent system
Physical state of the pure compound
Length of the column or TLC plate
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The purification of a compound using chromatography is dependent on several factors, including the solubility of the compound, the mobility or flow of the solvent system, and the length of the column or TLC plate. However, it is not typically dependent on the physical state of the pure compound. Here's why :

Option A : The solubility of the compound in the mobile phase and its interaction with the stationary phase are key factors in determining how the compound will migrate in a chromatographic system. Hence, the solubility of the compound does affect its purification.

Option B : The mobility or flow of the solvent system, often referred to as the mobile phase in chromatography, also plays a significant role in the separation of components in the mixture. The rate at which the mobile phase moves can influence how far and how quickly the components of the mixture will travel.

Option C : The physical state (solid, liquid, gas) of the pure compound is usually not a factor in the purification process in chromatography. Whether a compound is solid, liquid, or gas does not typically affect its ability to be separated by chromatography, as it is the interactions between the compound and the stationary/mobile phases that are key.

Option D : The length of the column or TLC plate can impact the degree of separation achieved in chromatography. A longer column or TLC plate can provide more opportunities for the interactions that drive the separation process, often leading to better separation of the components.

So, Option C is correct : The physical state of the pure compound is usually not a factor in its purification by chromatography.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text: The equivalents of ethylene diamine required to replace the neutral ligands from the coordination sphere of the trans-complex of CoCl$_{3} . 4NH_{3}$ is $_________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CoCl}{}_{3}\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}$; in the trans isomer the two Cl ligands are opposite each other and the four neutral ligands are $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$.

Ethylenediamine ($\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, en) is a neutral didentate ligand, so one en replaces two monodentate $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}+2\mathrm{en}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}+4\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$

Replacing all four $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ therefore needs 2 equivalents of en.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift

text:
For the reaction $A(g)⇌B(g)$ at 495 K, $\Delta_{r}$G${}^{\circ }$ = $-$9.478 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
If we start the reaction in a closed container at 495 K with 22 millimoles of A, the amount of B in the equilibrium mixture is $____________$ millimoles.
 (Round off to the Nearest Integer). [R = 8.314 J mol$^{-1} K^{-1}$; ln 10 = 2.303]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta G^{o} =$ $-$RT ln Keq

$-$9.478 $\times$ $10^{3} =$ $-$495 $\times$ 8.314 ln Keq

ln Keq = 2.303 = ln 10

So, Keq = 10

Now, A(g) $⇌$ B(g)

$\begin{array}{lll} t=0 & 22 & 0 \\ t=t & 22-x & x \end{array}$

$Keq=\frac{[B]}{[A]}=\frac{x}{(22-x)}=10$

x = 20

So, millimoles of B = 20

text:
When light of wavelength 248 nm falls on a metal of threshold energy 3.0 eV, the de-Broglie wavelength of emitted electrons is $_______A^{o}$. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[ Use : $\sqrt{3}$ = 1.73, h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$

$m_{e} = 9.1$ $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$; c = 3.0 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}$; 1eV = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19} J$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy of the incident photon:

$E=\dfrac{hc}{λ}=\dfrac{6.63\times 10^{-34}\times 3.0\times 10^{8}}{248\times 10^{-9}}=8.0\times 10^{-19}\text{J}(=5.0\text{eV})$

Threshold energy $W_{0}=3.0\text{eV}=3.0\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}=4.8\times 10^{-19}$ J, so the kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is

$K=E-W_{0}=8.0\times 10^{-19}-4.8\times 10^{-19}=3.2\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$

Momentum of the electron:

$p=\sqrt{2m_{e}K}=\sqrt{2\times 9.1\times 10^{-31}\times 3.2\times 10^{-19}}=7.63\times 10^{-25}\text{kg m s}^{-1}$

de Broglie wavelength:

$λ=\dfrac{h}{p}=\dfrac{6.63\times 10^{-34}}{7.63\times 10^{-25}}=8.7\times 10^{-10}\text{m}=8.7\text{Å}\approx 9\text{Å}$

Hence, the answer is 9.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 16th March Morning Shift
